subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What is meant by the term co-ordination number? Give the co-ordination number of atoms in a cubic close packed structure and in a body centred cubic structure.

verification.note: Unit 1 (Solid State) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.62-63, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The printed answer writes "in a 3d - crystal lattice", where 3d means three dimensional and not the 3d subshell; it is written out in full here. The values 12 for ccp and 8 for bcc are the book's own and are correct. SPELLING: the book prints "centered"; "centred" is used here to match the rest of the bank.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The co-ordination number of a particle is the
that touch it in a three dimensional crystal
Only the nearest neighbours are counted.
steps.why: The number counts touching neighbours only, which is why it measures how closely the particles are packed. Counting particles that are further away would give a number that has nothing to do with the packing.
common_mistakes: Counting all the particles in the unit cell. Only the nearest neighbours that touch the chosen particle are counted.
Confusing this with the co-ordination number of a complex ion. Here it is a packing count, not a count of ligands.
steps.memory_tip: Nearest and touching. Anything further away is not counted.
steps.margin_note: The words "nearest neighbouring particles" are the definition mark. Write them before the two numbers.

steps.label: The two values
lines: In ccp each atom touches 6 in its own layer,
In bcc the atom at the body centre touches
steps.why: The two counts come straight from the geometry. A close packed layer gives six neighbours in the plane and three in each neighbouring layer, so twelve in all. In a body centred cell the only atoms touching the central atom are the eight corner atoms.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two values. Cubic close packing gives 12 and body centred cubic gives 8.
Writing 6 for ccp. Six is only the count within one layer; the layers above and below add three each.
steps.memory_tip: Close packing is the tightest, so it gets the biggest number, 12. Body centred is looser, so 8.
steps.margin_note: Both numbers must appear. The one line breakdown 6 + 3 + 3 shows the examiner the 12 is not guessed.

insider_note: This question has two parts, so a definition alone can only earn one mark. Write 12 for ccp and 8 for bcc on the same line and label each.
